PEtab is the exchange format for ODE parameter estimation problems: an SBML model plus tables of
measurements, observables with noise models, conditions, and parameters with scales and bounds,
joined by a YAML file. This chapter writes the guide model at the best fit as a PEtab problem and
reads it back (`petab.R`); problems of the
[PEtab benchmark collection](https://github.com/Benchmarking-Initiative/Benchmark-Models-PEtab)
and other tools are read the same way.

## PEtab export

`exportPEtab()` writes reactions as SBML, observables, errors, data, and the transformation `p`
with scales, fixed values and values per condition. A parameter entering only as `exp()` is on
log scale. PEtab 2, the default, has no parameter scales: values are written on linear scale, with
a warning listing the log-scale parameters. The gauge of [Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html)
becomes fixed values, also linear.

- **State at rest.** With `steadyState = pSS`, each condition starts with a pre-equilibration to
  steady state before time 0. The totals of the conserved moieties (the `Pimpl()` parameters)
  become initial-value parameters: one species per total starts at the total, here complex
  `NfkIkb` for NFκB and unphosphorylated `Ikk` for IKK, all others at 0; the simulation preserves
  the totals. Both conditions differ only in the dose, given by the event, and share one
  pre-equilibration condition.
- **Event.** With `events = events`, the event at time 0 becomes the `TNF` value in the condition
  table, set after pre-equilibration.
- **Errors.** Imaging readouts get their error model; the blots, outside the error model, get the
  data standard deviations as noise parameters per measurement, as in `normL2()`.

```{r, include = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R", envir = new.env()))
```

```{r petabexport, warning = FALSE}
```

Each experiment starts with the pre-equilibration at $t = -\infty$, then the experiment condition at 0:

```{r}
read.delim("results/petab/experiments_oppelt.tsv")
read.delim("results/petab/conditions_oppelt.tsv")
```

## PEtab import

`importPEtab()` builds `prdfn`, the `obsfn`s of observables and errors, the `parfn` with the
scales of the parameter table, data and `objfn`. A pre-equilibration becomes a `Pimpl()` with
totals from the initial values. `options` go to the solver; with `compile = FALSE`, `compile()`
builds the sources.

```{r petabimport}
```

```{r petabcompile, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# all models of the chapter in one shared object
compile(g, x, pSS, p, e, petab$prd, petab$e, output = "oppelt_petab_guide", cores = 6)
```

```{r petabcompare}
```

The imported problem reproduces the data term of `model.R` at the best fit. `petab$bestfit` has
the nominal values on the problem scales, `petab$parlower` and `petab$parupper` the bounds; it is
fitted and profiled like any other.

## SBML models

`exportSbml()` writes species with compartments and volumes, reactions with kinetic laws,
parameters and initial assignments, here one species per total set to that total. SBML kinetic
laws are amounts per time: `exportSbml()` multiplies concentration rates by the compartment
volume, `importSbml()` divides again. `importSbml()` returns a list: the equation list with
compartments and volumes in `reactions`, parameter values, initial values, observables, assignment
rules and events:

```{r}
sbml <- importSbml("results/petab/oppelt.xml")
names(sbml)
c(states = length(sbml$reactions$states), reactions = length(sbml$reactions$rates))
identical(sort(sbml$reactions$states), sort(reactions$states))
```

`exportSbml(reactions, parameters, inits, filepath)` writes an equation list without PEtab tables.

## Formats and limits

- SBML and PEtab run through reticulate with `python-libsbml`; `DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON` selects the
  interpreter.
- PEtab 1 and 2 are read. `exportPEtab()` writes 2 by default, 1 with `formatVersion = "1"`, which
  keeps scales but puts expressions into the condition table that only dMod2 reads.
- `exportPEtab()` writes events at time 0 that replace a state and refuses others.

Reference: `exportPEtab()`, `importPEtab()`, `exportSbml()`, `importSbml()`
